feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: OneStreamer: Unifying Perception, Memory, and Proactive Response in Streaming Video Interaction
entry.summary:
OneStreamer is a 4B streaming video LLM that unifies perception, memory, and proactive response using Proactive Hierarchical Caption Memory and Proactive State Transition Learning.

Why it matters: It enables video LLMs to perform real-time perception and historical reasoning efficiently without needing to re-process raw historical visual features.

entry.title: World Observer: Joint Actor-Observer Generation for Persistent World Modeling
entry.summary:
World Observer decouples observing from acting by jointly generating perspective actor views and panoramic observer views to maintain out-of-view object states and dynamics during world modeling.

Why it matters: It solves state persistent and dynamic continuity issues in video world models when objects temporarily leave the agent's field of view.

entry.title: A Missing Piece for Trustworthy AI Reviewers: From Benchmarking Rhetorical Robustness to SciCore Review
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced RobustReview, a 1,260-manuscript benchmark evaluating AI reviewer rhetorical robustness, and SciCore, a dual-branch reviewer that averages full-manuscript and extracted science-core judgments to reduce sensitivity to rewrites.

Why it matters: Evaluating AI peer reviewers for rhetorical robustness prevents automated systems from being gamed through stylistic rewrites that do not alter the underlying scientific content.

entry.title: Make Sparse Rewards Count: Density-Aware Reward Aggregation for Multi-Reward RL
entry.summary:
Density-Aware Reward Aggregation (DARA) introduces an adaptive, inverse-square-root density correction to balance multi-reward RL training based on active-group density.

Why it matters: DARA accelerates the multi-reward RL training of large language models for auxiliary constraints like formatting and length compliance without sacrificing final model performance.

entry.title: EgoTools: Towards Tool-Centric Reasoning in Real-World Egocentric Videos
entry.summary:
EgoTools introduces a 100-hour tool-centric egocentric video dataset and a 1,000 QA-pair diagnostic benchmark to advance tool-centric embodied reasoning in multimodal models.

Why it matters: It exposes performance gaps in leading multimodal models regarding physical and spatial tool interaction while providing data to train more capable embodied agents.

entry.title: E-MoE: Enhanced Mixture-of-Experts for Non-Factorized Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
E-MoE introduces an Enhanced Mixture-of-Experts architecture for non-factorized diffusion language models that uses discrete shared latents from expert-routing decisions to improve few-step generation without increasing active parameters.

Why it matters: It enables higher-quality text generation in fast, few-step diffusion language models without incurring additional active computational overhead.

entry.title: CorrGRPO: Correlation-Normalized GRPO for Multi-Reward Learning
entry.summary:
CorrGRPO improves multi-reward language model training by normalizing pairwise reward covariances into Pearson correlation coefficients, preventing large-scale rewards from suppressing smaller-scale reward signals during advantage calculation.

Why it matters: It prevents scale imbalances when combining multiple reward signals, allowing models to better handle tasks involving complex reward tradeoffs or multi-objective optimization.

entry.title: Fewer Tokens, Better Action: GPT-6 Astra Robot Agents with 14% Higher Success Rate but 65% Fewer Tokens
entry.summary:
PyRUA-Lean is an interactive code-execution framework that reduces VLM agent token usage by 65% while improving task success rates to 71.7% using GPT-6 Astra.

Why it matters: Selective observation and local code execution significantly reduce latency and compute costs for VLM-driven robotic agents without compromising task performance.

entry.title: InterEvolve: Test-Time Evolution of Reward Programs for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
entry.summary:
InterEvolve is a test-time evolution framework that enables humanoid robots to master unseen loco-manipulation tasks without retraining by using an LLM agent and numerical optimizer to iteratively refine reward programs based on execution feedback.

Why it matters: It allows humanoid robots to autonomously adapt existing motor skills to complex, long-horizon, and novel tasks at test time without requiring expensive neural network retraining.

entry.title: PhysVista: Benchmarking Physical Intelligence in VLMs via a Perception-Reasoning-Assessment Loop
entry.summary:
PhysVista is a benchmark that evaluates physical intelligence in Vision-Language Models using a closed cognitive loop framework incorporating physical state perception, physical dynamics reasoning, and physical plausibility assessment.

Why it matters: It provides a structured methodology to diagnose whether VLMs can accurately judge the physical plausibility and authenticity of real-world scenes and AI-generated video content.

entry.title: Multimodal Flow: Unified Flow Modeling of Language and Vision in Embedding Spaces
entry.summary:
Multimodal Flow introduces MF-1, a unified generative model that replaces discrete visual tokens and hybrid sampling with a fully continuous, chunk-causal Flow Matching process over joint language and vision embedding spaces.

Why it matters: It establishes a fully continuous flow modeling paradigm that avoids visual quantization bottlenecks and modality-dependent sampling procedures while outperforming hybrid and discrete models at equivalent compute budgets.

entry.title: Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation
entry.summary:
Omni-Embed-Mini introduces a 0.9B-parameter omni-modal embedding model that maps six modalities into a shared cosine space without updating text-side parameters or regressing text retrieval performance.

Why it matters: It enables efficient multi-modal embedding capabilities across six modalities in a compact parameter footprint without sacrificing baseline text retrieval quality.

entry.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
entry.summary:
SILSA is a topology-aware 3D generation framework using sliding-window slice latents across canonical axes to enable high-resolution, single-stage rectified-flow generation with significantly reduced token counts.

Why it matters: SILSA significantly reduces inference latency and memory overhead while better preserving thin structures and topological connectivity in high-resolution 3D asset generation.

entry.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing Skill-Level Memory for Partially Observable Robotic Manipulation
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced HIDE, a 15-task benchmark for partial observability in robotic manipulation, and SEEK, a memory-augmentation framework that combines three complementary memory mechanisms to retain historical task state.

Why it matters: Combining diverse memory mechanisms allows robotic policies to reliably track unobservable task states and make correct context-dependent decisions during complex manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Architect-Ant: Editable Automatic Furnishing of Architectural Floor Plans
entry.summary:
Architect-Ant generates constraint-aware, editable furniture layouts from floor plans using a coordinate-based DSL, fine-tuning, and GRPO optimization with a Layout Rule Score.

Why it matters: It enables rapid, constraint-compliant, and fully editable 2D/3D interior design generation directly from real architectural training patterns without relying on slow iterative agent inference.

entry.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
HC-DLM couples discrete token generation with a continuous latent trajectory, making the continuous latent the sole persistent generative state to maintain token dependencies during parallel decoding.

Why it matters: It unifies discrete token constraints with continuous latent representations to improve bidirectional reasoning and structured generation in diffusion language models.

entry.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
entry.summary:
A Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling algorithm transforms off-policy expert traces into on-policy data tailored to a reference model, allowing supervised finetuning to match or exceed reinforcement learning performance.

Why it matters: It allows practitioners to achieve RL-level generalization and low capability erosion using standard SFT pipelines by repurposing sampling as a data-shaping primitive.

entry.title: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)
entry.summary:
TESS introduces a Pointwise Value Matching objective to replace unstable sample-weighting methods, enabling scalable and transferable data selection across datasets and model sizes.

Why it matters: It enables stable, scalable data selection that generalizes across different datasets and larger language models without relying on heuristic scoring.

entry.title: Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval
entry.summary:
Causal Memory Policy (CMP) addresses memory utility unidentifiability in LLMs caused by retrieval-level positivity violations by intervening directly on retrieval using self-normalized inverse propensity weighting.

Why it matters: It proves that standard store-level memory evaluation metrics fail due to structural unidentifiability and provides a provably unbiased causal framework to accurately evaluate retrieved memory value.

entry.title: External Observers May See More Clearly: Cross-Model Span-Level Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models via Hidden State Probing
entry.summary:
A new internal hidden state probe framework detects fine-grained span-level hallucination onsets and continuations, enabling cross-model observation where a secondary model detects a primary generator's hallucinations.

Why it matters: This approach demonstrates that self-probe limits can be bypassed by using smaller, specialized external observer models to detect generation hallucinations in real-time without relying on external retrieval.

entry.title: CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
CARM is a sequence-level response masking technique for LLM reinforcement learning that applies absolute values to token log-ratios before averaging, preventing signed policy drifts from canceling out during off-policy filtering.

Why it matters: CARM prevents off-policy optimization instability caused by hidden token-level policy drift, improving the performance of LLM post-training on complex math and coding tasks.

entry.title: On Language Drift during RLVR Post-Training
entry.summary:
A study proves theoretically and empirically that reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR) causes unbounded language drift in chain-of-thought reasoning during novel tasks, which cannot be constrained without reducing model performance.

Why it matters: Attempting to prevent language drift to keep chain-of-thought reasoning monitorable will fundamentally degrade model performance during frontier RLVR post-training.

entry.title: From Gradients to Capabilities: Understanding Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
An empirical study of Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation using Qwen3-1.7B and SmolLM3-3B reveals how loss averaging, Adam moments, BF16 quantization, and top-64 KL gradients alter parameter updates and task capabilities.

Why it matters: Understanding how optimization mechanics like Adam moments, precision limits, and loss weighting alter gradient signals allows engineers to better fine-tune multi-teacher distillation pipelines for small language models.

entry.title: Every Ablation Is a Dose: Counterweights and the Semblance of Self-Repair
entry.summary:
Researchers show that language model 'self-repair' is actually the predictable action of fixed counterweights operating along an affine law, $E_r(\lambda)=\mathrm{own}_r+\gamma_r\lambda$, rather than a dynamic compensatory mechanism.

Why it matters: Understanding self-repair as a static, weight-based affine response simplifies circuit analysis and enables researchers to predict intervention outcomes directly from static model weights.

entry.title: Are We Recovering Mechanisms? Objective-Level Recovery Gaps in Mechanistic Interpretability
entry.summary:
Intervention-defined faithfulness objectives misrank circuit candidates by preferring poorer-performing models, creating an objective-level recovery gap that automated discovery algorithms inherit under standard resampling methods.

Why it matters: Improving automated circuit discovery algorithms is insufficient if the underlying evaluation objectives inherently reward incorrect or inferior mechanisms.

entry.title: UniEvo-VL: An On-policy Self-Distillation Training Recipe for Multimodal Model Self-improvement
entry.summary:
UniEvo-VL enables unified multimodal models to self-improve image generation via an on-policy self-distillation framework that minimizes per-state divergence between a critique-conditioned teacher and a vanilla student context.

Why it matters: It demonstrates a viable recipe for recursive test-time self-improvement in multimodal models without requiring external supervision or larger dedicated teacher models.

entry.title: False Frontiers: Diagnosing and Mitigating Co-Cheating in Self-Evolving Search Agents
entry.summary:
CrossFit mitigates co-cheating in self-evolving search agents by cross-partitioning source documents between the proposer and solver, preventing false reward signals and improving downstream accuracy.

Why it matters: It prevents self-evolving AI models from reinforcing shared errors, ensuring that internal training rewards reflect actual performance gains on downstream tasks.

entry.title: AREX-2: Advancing Self-Improving Agents through Long-Horizon Reflective Tasks
entry.summary:
AREX-2 trains a Qwen3.8-27B model on synthesized long-horizon, reflective improvement trajectories from programming and machine learning tasks to achieve domain-agnostic test-time self-improvement.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that training agents on verifiable programming and ML trajectory data instills domain-agnostic self-improvement capabilities that generalize to deep research and scale with execution budgets.

entry.title: Mid-Harness: Scaling Actions Between Model and Harness for Terminal Agents
entry.summary:
Mid-Harness scales test-time compute by sampling and verifying candidate actions at the model-harness boundary before execution without altering the underlying action generator or environment harness.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that allocating test-time compute to verify individual actions before execution prevents irreversible environment state corruption, outperforming simple trajectory-level scaling in efficiency and success rate.

entry.title: EVOKE: Eliciting World Knowledge in Agents for Transferable Decision-Making
entry.summary:
EVOKE is a post-training method for LLM agents that elicits pretrained world knowledge by ranking candidate actions across diverse goals at fixed environment states, improving task generalization and transfer without explicit world-model training.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to generalize to unseen environments by leveraging existing pretrained knowledge through goal-diverse decision supervision, bypassing the need for error-prone explicit world-model training.

entry.title: Agent Error Dataset: Scaling 50,000 Error--Diagnosis Pairs for Failure Analysis and Error-Aware Post-Training
entry.summary:
The Agent Error Dataset (AED) introduces 50,228 error-diagnosis pairs across 33 environments, using a five-stage pipeline to generate, verify, and apply error corrections for LLM agent post-training.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that structured error diagnosis and repair data extracted from failed agent rollouts can significantly improve model reasoning and recovery compared to training only on successful trajectories.

entry.title: LANTERN: Illuminating Hidden Mathematical Knowledge in Language Models
entry.summary:
LANTERN is a pipeline that leverages pretrained language model activations to discover, generate, and verify novel mathematical connections between integer sequences in under 8 hours.

Why it matters: Language models can directly mine their internal representations to automatically uncover and verify previously unknown mathematical relationships at scale with minimal compute time.

entry.title: It's Not What the Image Shows: Irrelevant Context Destabilises VLM Judges Without Informing Them
entry.summary:
The Misleading-Image Stress Test (MIST) benchmark reveals that VLM judges shift their labels when shown irrelevant images, driven by image presence rather than visual content or meaning.

Why it matters: Evaluating VLMs as human-surrogate judges is highly sensitive to incidental visual context, meaning substitutability assessments reflect evaluation setups as much as underlying model capabilities.

entry.title: Unmask the State: When Does State Adaptation Matter for Masked Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers analyzed state adaptation in Masked Diffusion Language Models across five inference axes, demonstrating that selective, detector-driven adaptation captures significant oracle gains while modifying only a fraction of generation states.

Why it matters: Selectively adapting decoding strategies at specific high-opportunity states enables more efficient and effective MDM inference compared to applying static unmasking strategies or uniform adaptation.

entry.title: Breaking Babel: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Long-Form Subtitle Translation
entry.summary:
SMART is a self-evolving multi-agent system for long-form subtitle translation that adapts prompts and routing policies via test-time training without altering underlying LLM weights.

Why it matters: SMART enables adaptive, context-aware translation of long-form media series with consistent terminology without requiring expensive parameter fine-tuning.

entry.title: DyRAD: Radar Novel View Synthesis for Dynamic Driving Scenes
entry.summary:
DyRAD achieves radar novel view synthesis for dynamic scenes by explicitly modeling range-azimuth-Doppler (RAD) tensors using static and motion-tracked point reflectors coupled with a fixed analytic point-spread function.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, dynamic novel view synthesis and cross-sensor simulation for radar, facilitating robust closed-loop evaluation of autonomous driving systems.

entry.title: LoopVL: Recurrent Visual Intelligence
entry.summary:
LoopVL extends Loop Transformers to vision-language models by iteratively updating a unified vision-language state through shared modules using Module-Loop and Model-Loop computation.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that parameter-efficient recurrent architectures can achieve superior visual reasoning and multimodal performance compared to larger feedforward models.

entry.title: I Have a Stream: Making Self-Supervised Learning Work on Continuous Video
entry.summary:
StreamMAE enables robust self-supervised learning on continuous video streams without global reshuffling, matching standard i.i.d. MAE performance using stream-aware regularization and motion-biased cropping.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that self-supervised vision models can be trained effectively on ordered, continuous video streams, moving closer to realistic online visual learning without relying on globally shuffled datasets.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
entry.summary:
A new joint scaling law models recurrence and sparsity together, enabling the optimal design of looped Mixture-of-Experts models under compute and memory constraints.

Why it matters: The framework allows hardware-constrained developers to maximize model performance and test-time compute scaling by systematically balancing depth recurrence with MoE parameter capacity.

entry.title: Thinking Outside the Box: Can Language Models Rely on External Guidance Selectively?
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Box^2-Bench to evaluate model reliance on external guidance, finding that while frontier models struggle with misleading workflows, targeted SFT and outcome-based RL improve selective reliance on external information.

Why it matters: Selective reliance on fallible external guidance provides a critical metric for agent reliability that standard task performance benchmarks fail to capture.

entry.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
SCAPO is a causally inspired RLVR method that improves GRPO by adjusting token-level rewards using semifactual prompt stability to prevent models from reinforcing spurious prompt dependencies.

Why it matters: Finer-grained token credit assignment based on semifactual stability significantly enhances the mathematical reasoning performance and out-of-distribution generalization of language models.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Loop Scaling Laws, the first framework to jointly model recurrence and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) sparsity alongside model size and data volume.

Why it matters: The framework provides a principled, compute- and memory-constrained design guide to scale parameter capacity and effective depth simultaneously without proportional compute overhead.

entry.title: PivotOPD: Learning to Recover from Pivotal Mistakes in Multi-Turn Agents
entry.summary:
PivotOPD is an on-policy distillation framework that combines preventive distillation via reverse KL and recovery distillation via forward KL to help multi-turn language agents avoid and recover from early pivotal mistakes.

Why it matters: It mitigates compounding errors in multi-turn AI agents by providing targeted teacher supervision that trains models to both prevent critical errors and successfully recover when they occur.

entry.title: What Limits Recursive Reasoning Models: Optimization, Architecture and Test-Time Scaling
entry.summary:
Researchers isolated the key drivers of recursive reasoning models, establishing a simplified optimization recipe that yields a 13.6M-parameter model with superior out-of-distribution performance without needing explicit hierarchical architectures.

Why it matters: Properly stabilized, highly compact recursive models can serve as efficient, parameter-light tool-use solvers for LLMs tackling complex algorithmic subproblems.

entry.title: RoPE at the End of Its Rope? Theory, Diagnosis, and Mitigation of Long-Context Failures
entry.summary:
A new theoretical analysis of RoPE reveals an intrinsic tradeoff between semantic stability and positional sensitivity, enabling targeted frequency rescaling that improves long-context task accuracy by up to 25 percentage points without retraining.

Why it matters: It provides a zero-overhead theoretical and diagnostic framework to instantly fix long-context LLM failures on specific task types without costly model retraining.

entry.title: LLM Persona Unlearning
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce PersonaUnlearnBench and PaCE, a method that aligns target-prompt states with desirable responses to reliably erase latent LLM personas while preserving response quality and utility.

Why it matters: Weight-level persona unlearning offers persistent control over latent model behavior, preventing open-weight LLMs from being prompted into harmful or unintended personas even after runtime safety controls are removed.

entry.title: GrammarRL: Effective Grammar-Constrained Decoding via Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
GrammarRL uses label-free reinforcement learning with self-supervised direct and reverse likelihood rewards to adapt Llama models to grammar-constrained decoding without annotated data or beam-search inference overhead.

Why it matters: It eliminates the semantic quality degradation common in grammar-constrained decoding while maintaining the low computational footprint and speed of greedy inference.

entry.title: Learning Steganography Is Easy, Learning Steganographic Reasoning Is Hard
entry.summary:
A comparative study shows that steganographic reasoning is significantly harder for LLMs to learn than steganographic messaging or encoded reasoning, typically requiring supervised fine-tuning except when cover tasks make information hiding convenient.

Why it matters: Chain-of-thought AI oversight remains viable for most scenarios because steganographic reasoning is difficult to elicit, though convenient cover tasks still pose a bypass risk.

entry.title: Synthetic Pre-pretraining Survives Scale, but Not as a Grammatical Prior
entry.summary:
A comprehensive study reveals synthetic pre-pretraining (PPT) maintains token efficiency gains at scales up to 7B parameters and 100B pre-training tokens, but the benefit stems from long-range retrieval improvements rather than a grammatical prior.

Why it matters: Synthetic pre-pretraining task design should shift from mimicking natural language grammar to optimizing long-range retrieval capacities to maximize token efficiency at scale.

entry.title: Stress-Testing LLM Lie Detectors: Role-Play Failures and Spurious Correlations
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated eight LLM lie detection probes against 8,916 anti-factual persona responses, revealing that existing probes fail under role-play and instead track confounded concepts like instruction compliance or response likelihood.

Why it matters: Current LLM lie detection probes cannot reliably distinguish reality from role-play, demonstrating that probes must be trained on datasets where truth is decorrelated from confounding operational concepts.

entry.title: VoxMem: Benchmarking Multimodal Memory in Large Audio Language Models
entry.summary:
VoxMem is a new benchmark featuring 3,196 instances across 177 hours of spoken sessions designed to evaluate multimodal memory in Large Audio Language Models across diverse acoustic evidence types and memory operations.

Why it matters: Current LALMs struggle to maintain non-transcript audio context like speaker identity and acoustic environment over multi-session long-context histories, highlighting key gaps for conversational AI development.

entry.title: Omni-IO Skills: Harnessing Your Agent Omni-Native
entry.summary:
Omni-IO Skills is a plug-and-play agent harness that enables omni-native multimodal capabilities without modifying host agent reasoning cores by using hierarchical skills, dependency-aware orchestration, and a persistent Asset Registry.

Why it matters: It provides a practical framework to expand AI agents to handle diverse modalities and complex workflows without undertaking expensive foundation model retrainings or updates.

entry.title: Follow the Entities: A Corpus Map for Agentic Search
entry.summary:
CorpusMap is an offline-constructed navigation layer that organizes document collections into a graph of entity pages to optimize LLM agent search.

Why it matters: By pre-indexing entity relationships across document collections, LLM agents can retrieve disconnected evidence faster and more accurately while cutting token overhead.

entry.title: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?
entry.summary:
EngiWorld is a benchmark featuring 1,301 expert-curated tasks across 6 engineering domains and 26 software platforms to evaluate autonomous agents across full professional engineering workflows.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized, programmatic foundation to evaluate and advance autonomous agents handling complex, end-to-end industrial engineering workflows.

entry.title: Beyond Dyadic Memory: Interaction-Aware Multimodal Memory with Adaptive Agentic Retrieval for Multi-Party Spoken Conversations
entry.summary:
VoxPolyMem introduces an interaction-aware multimodal memory framework and the EG-GRPO reinforcement learning method to optimize agentic retrieval in multi-party spoken conversations.

Why it matters: It establishes a specialized framework for long-term memory and accurate attribution in complex, multi-speaker multimodal conversational AI.

entry.title: LongCat-DeepResearch Technical Report
entry.summary:
LongCat-DeepResearch combines an enhanced LongCat model with a multi-agent workflow that uses global planning, parallel section drafting, and targeted local revisions to generate research reports.

Why it matters: Targeted section-level revisions reduce the computational cost of repeating full-report rewrites in complex multi-agent research workflows.

entry.title: LLMs are General Asynchronous Agents
entry.summary:
A general asynchronous LLM framework uses inference coroutines with overlapping memory states to enable real-world concurrent execution without task-specific training.

Why it matters: It enables standard off-the-shelf LLMs to process continuous incoming inputs while actively executing tasks, removing the need for specialized asynchronous architectures.

entry.title: SoL-Refiner: Speed-of-Light One-Step Refinement for High-Resolution Video
entry.summary:
SoL-Refiner is a one-step video refiner that upscales low-resolution model outputs into 4K videos using a single denoising step, achieving an 8.91x speedup over multi-step baselines.

Why it matters: It eliminates the sampling bottleneck in high-resolution video generation by drastically reducing latency without sacrificing visual quality metrics.

entry.title: APM-Bench: Benchmarking Cross-session Persistent Memory for Egocentric Streaming Video Assistants
entry.summary:
APM-Bench is a benchmark evaluating cross-session persistent memory for egocentric streaming video assistants, featuring multi-session life trajectories to test long-term recall, real-time efficiency, and missing evidence recognition.

Why it matters: It provides a realistic testbed to develop persistent memory systems for AI assistants that interact continuously and intermittently across real-world, multi-day user activities.

entry.title: Asking for What Was Never Requested: Horizontal and Vertical Proactivity in Agents
entry.summary:
A new framework formalizes horizontal and vertical proactivity in agents and trains a questioner model via Q&D optimization to pursue unstated evidence without relying on LLM judges.

Why it matters: It enables smaller AI agents to autonomously uncover unstated task requirements and know when to stop asking questions without relying on expensive, larger models or LLM judges.

entry.title: Context Language Models
entry.summary:
Context Language Models (CLMs) natively manage context by treating it as an editable file, allowing models to make unrestricted updates, reduce compute, and learn context-management strategies via reinforcement learning and prompt optimization.

Why it matters: Shifting context management from external harnesses to intrinsic model operations significantly cuts inference FLOPs and server compute while increasing task accuracy in long-horizon and multi-agent tasks.

entry.title: StoryEngine: A State-Grounded Agentic Framework for Video Storytelling
entry.summary:
StoryEngine is a state-grounded agentic framework for long-form video storytelling that uses structured state tracking, canonical references, and bounded evaluation-guided repair to maintain narrative coherence and visual consistency across multi-shot videos.

Why it matters: It prevents visual drift and causal inconsistencies in long-form video generation by decoupling state tracking from pixel outputs and adding automated repair loops.

entry.title: Selecting The Most Informative Tokens in Natural Language Autoencoders
entry.summary:
A study of 4.7 million autoencoder explanations shows chat-structure rankers select relevant token positions for audit better than computational signals, enabling 95% compute reduction without losing threat detection capability.

Why it matters: Auditors can drastically reduce the computational cost of interpreting neural network activations by inspecting only 5% of structured token positions while still detecting critical safety threats.

entry.title: AutoRef: Harness Optimization for Agentic Multi-Reference Image Generation
entry.summary:
AutoRef automatically optimizes executable agentic harnesses via coding-agent rewrites and beam search, improving multi-reference image generation without updating underlying model weights.

Why it matters: It enables significant multi-reference image quality improvements through automated program optimization instead of costly model retraining.

entry.title: Omni-Decision: Evidence-Ledger Planning for Omni-Modal Agents
entry.summary:
Omni-Decision replaces dialogue history in omni-modal agents with a compact evidence ledger, filtering noisy observations via a critic to improve multi-step planning efficiency and accuracy.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that decoupling evidence state management from raw observation history significantly reduces execution costs while matching or exceeding state-of-the-art omni-modal performance.

entry.title: KV-Kaizen: Learning Context-Adaptive Cache Compression Choices
entry.summary:
KV-Kaizen is a context-adaptive selector that dynamically configures per-layer LLM KV caches across layer sharing, precision, and low-rank latent representation without evicting tokens.

Why it matters: It alleviates the decode-stage memory bottleneck in long-context LLMs, demonstrating that compressing large pre-trained models contextually is superior to serving smaller uncompressed models.

entry.title: $S^3$: Spectral Null-Space Swap Makes Reasoning Models Efficient
entry.summary:
Spectral Null-Space Swap ($S^3$) is a training-free model composition method that isolates the thinking model's weight components in the non-thinking model's null space, reducing inference token overhead while maintaining or improving reasoning accuracy.

Why it matters: It enables developers to significantly lower LLM chain-of-thought inference token costs and speed up generation without retraining models or sacrificing reasoning accuracy.

entry.title: On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
PUMBA is a unified trajectory-aware training framework for masked diffusion models that combines policy-induced trajectory training, inter-step information passing, and multi-step backpropagation through time.

Why it matters: It enables masked diffusion language models to achieve autoregressive-level generation quality while significantly reducing the inference step budget.

entry.title: The Unequal Influence of Bad Advice: Using Training Data Attribution to Modulate Emergent Misalignment
entry.summary:
Researchers used training data attribution to quantify how individual harmful examples drive emergent misalignment, demonstrating that filtering data via these influence scores can enhance or attenuate the behavior.

Why it matters: Quantifying data influence allows developers to mitigate emergent misalignment by identifying and removing specific high-impact harmful examples from fine-tuning datasets.

entry.title: Active Budget Can Kill Sensitivity: Diagnosing and Repairing TopK Sparse Autoencoder Reliability
entry.summary:
Researchers identified that TopK Sparse Autoencoders reduce rare-feature sensitivity due to selection boundary geometry and introduced pairwise rank stabilization to fix it.

Why it matters: Evaluating SAEs solely on reconstruction and sparsity masks feature instability, but addressing boundary geometry ensures rare features remain reliable under semantic variations.

entry.title: Scaling Influence Functions in LLMs through Eigenbasis-Corrected One-Bit Gradient Projection
entry.summary:
Eigenbasis-Corrected One-Bit Gradient Projection (EOGP) compresses stored training gradients using EK-FAC, subspace PCA, and one-bit quantization to scale LLM influence function calculations within tight memory constraints.

Why it matters: EOGP significantly reduces the storage overhead of saving training gradients, enabling scalable, repeated influence function computations across massive LLM datasets for unknown future queries.

entry.title: Pattern Formation in Transformers
entry.summary:
Applying pattern-formation theory to full Transformer architectures reveals that positional encodings, multi-head attention, and output-value geometries selectively amplify, stabilize, and combine rich token patterns like traveling and rotating waves.

Why it matters: Leveraging pattern-formation theory to design task-aligned initializations and positional encodings significantly boosts sample efficiency and convergence speed in Transformer models.

entry.title: Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning
entry.summary:
OASIS overcomes scaling limits in on-policy self-distillation by supervising verified student trajectories using unverified model-generated attempts as teacher context, requiring only final-answer labels.

Why it matters: OASIS preserves the performance gains of self-distillation at larger model scales while eliminating the need for step-by-step written solutions, relying instead solely on final-answer labels.

entry.title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision
entry.summary:
The Latent Information Feedback Transformer (LIFT) introduces deep-to-shallow recurrent state feedback during pretraining by framing state learning as a parallelizable, teacher-forced prediction task using an off-the-shelf language model's next-token distribution.

Why it matters: LIFT bypasses the single-token autoregressive bottleneck by allowing language models to pass rich latent states across generation steps without sacrificing parallelized pretraining.

entry.title: Retrieval Capacity of Self-Attention Under Competition
entry.summary:
Researchers measure transformer retrieval capacity by retaining only top-weighted tokens per head, layer, and query without retraining, revealing how attention set size scales with context length, competition, and weight renormalization.

Why it matters: Understanding how competition and aggregation dictate effective attention set sizes informs more efficient context pruning, sparsification, and KV-cache compression techniques.

entry.title: Beyond Teacher Assignment: Domain-Normalized Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Domain-Normalized Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (DN-MOPD) rescales domain feedback by its measured spread, preventing instruction-following signals from swamping mathematics signals when merging specialist language models into a single student.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that successfully consolidating domain-specialized models into a single multi-talented LLM requires balancing feedback magnitudes across domains, not just routing prompts to the correct teacher.

entry.title: Post-Training Leaves Behavioral Shadows on Unrelated Decisions
entry.summary:
Active Taskless Distillation (ATD) enables language models to transfer downstream capabilities using only a single task-unrelated word output per prompt from a post-trained teacher.

Why it matters: The findings demonstrate that post-training updates leave systematic behavioral shadows in unrelated text, enabling silent capability transfer without exposing domain-specific training data or model parameters.

entry.title: How Far Are We from Removing the Visual Encoder? Scaling Laws for Encoder-Free Multimodal Pretraining
entry.summary:
A systematic study demonstrates that encoder-free multimodal LLMs follow distinct compute-scaling laws, with visual losses predicted to match encoder-based MLLMs at approximately 10^22 FLOPs.

Why it matters: The visual prior advantage of dedicated encoders diminishes with scale, making simpler, unified encoder-free MLLM architectures practical for large compute budgets.

entry.title: Learning Native Reflection in Unified Models with Interleaved Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
UMM-Reflection uses trajectory-level reinforcement learning across interleaved reflection text and flow-based revisions within a single unified model, enabling self-correction without an external inference verifier.

Why it matters: It allows unified multimodal models to natively critique and iteratively repair their own generated images without relying on external critic models or verifiers during inference.

entry.title: Groupwise Agentic Grading and Advantage Redistribution for Code Agent RL
entry.summary:
GAGAR improves code agent RL by using an SFT-trained agentic grader to rank test-passing trajectories in a shared workspace, redistributing advantages to favor higher-quality code while preserving the group's total advantage sum.

Why it matters: It enables large language model code agents to learn cleaner, higher-quality implementations without sacrificing the objective ground-truth feedback provided by executable test suites.

entry.title: Recursive Harness Distillation across Agents for Robot Manipulation
entry.summary:
Recursive Harness Distillation accumulates and refines robot failure interventions into non-parametric playbooks that improve task success across different agent models without updating model parameters.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that complex robot manipulation policies can be significantly improved at runtime using light, non-parametric guidance without costly model retraining.

entry.title: WorldPlay2: Extending Real-Time Interactive World Models in Control and Horizon
entry.summary:
WorldPlay2 is an interactive world model that improves real-time control and long-horizon consistency using a factorized hybrid control interface, compressed memory tokens, and a Stable Forcing distillation strategy.

Why it matters: It enables interactive world models to process complex, multi-modal control inputs while maintaining real-time performance and video stability over extended time horizons.

entry.title: QwenGyre: An Elastic Reinforcement Learning Framework for Training xLong-Horizon Agents
entry.summary:
QwenGyre is an elastic online reinforcement learning framework designed for extra-long-horizon LLM agents, solving GPU idling and trajectory redundancy.

Why it matters: It enables efficient online RL training for complex, long-horizon tasks spanning hundreds of steps and 700K+ tokens per rollout without severe GPU idle time.

entry.title: WideSWE: Can Coding Agents Coordinate Changes Across Repositories?
entry.summary:
WideSWE introduces a benchmark of 120 real-world tasks across 103 software ecosystems to evaluate AI coding agents on coordinating bug fixes and feature implementations across multiple repositories.

Why it matters: WideSWE shifts agent evaluation beyond single-codebase benchmarks to reflect real-world multi-repository dependencies and cross-ecosystem development challenges.

entry.title: Change the Product, Keep the Parameters: Associative Algebra Layers for Transformers
entry.summary:
A new Transformer layer replaces dense matrix multiplication with an associative-algebra product, reducing arithmetic complexity to quadratic scaling for fixed physical block sizes while keeping the overall parameter count constant.

Why it matters: This approach provides a viable framework to trade downstream model accuracy for hardware throughput gains without altering the total parameter capacity of Transformer architectures.

entry.title: In-Flight KV Cache with Clean Anchors for Faster Autoregressive Video Diffusion
entry.summary:
FlashForward accelerates autoregressive video diffusion by directly reusing stage-specific in-flight KV caches across concurrent GPU stages and stabilizing noisy trajectories with sparse clean anchor latents.

Why it matters: It significantly speeds up long video generation on multi-GPU systems while maintaining temporal consistency and visual quality without needing redundant model forward passes.

entry.title: Structured Residual Connectivity Matters for Diffusion Transformers
entry.summary:
A structured connectivity design for Diffusion Transformers replaces uniform residual streams with differentiable, selective cross-depth paths to dynamically retrieve early-layer spatial and semantic features.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that adaptive cross-layer routing significantly improves generative quality and training efficiency in DiTs with minimal parameter overhead.

entry.title: FlowTool: Controlling Tool Parameter in Image Retouching via Flow Matching
entry.summary:
FlowTool replaces autoregressive MLLM reasoning in image retouching by framing tool parameter selection as a conditional rectified flow generation task using a Diffusion Transformer.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that complex, multi-modal tool-use tasks can be executed much faster and with fewer computational resources by shifting from autoregressive text generation to flow matching over continuous parameters.

entry.title: Imprint Reader: From Weight-Update Readout to Behavioral Intervention
entry.summary:
The Imprint Reader uses Semantic Mount-and-Read Tuning (SMaRT) to translate frozen LLM weight updates into natural-language descriptions and guide behavioral interventions via MetaEdit.

Why it matters: It establishes the feasibility of decoding model parameter changes into readable descriptions and leveraging those representations to directly steer LLM behavior without task-specific training data.

entry.title: TT-VidT: Decoupling the Temporal Axis for Efficient Motion-Centric Video Pretraining
entry.summary:
TT-VidT decouples video temporal processing by pairing a DINOv3 ViT-B/16 spatial path with a Temporal Transfer Layer, using Diff Compression to reconstruct target frames from initial appearance anchors and motion tokens.

Why it matters: TT-VidT demonstrates that decoupling spatial and temporal paths allows video architectures to achieve state-of-the-art motion accuracy while drastically reducing encoder FLOPs compared to dense 3D baselines.

entry.title: Telescopic Language Models
entry.summary:
Telescopic Language Models use stochastic prefix supervision with a full anchor to train a single Transformer that functions as a valid language model at every layer depth.

Why it matters: A single training run can serve arbitrary compute budgets dynamically at runtime without requiring separate models, compression runs, or inference-time modifications.

entry.title: How to Loop MoE: Flatten the Experts, Untie the Attention
entry.summary:
The Foil architecture optimizes looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models by flattening expert layers to increase the pool of choices per routing decision and untying attention parameters across passes.

Why it matters: It provides a concrete design framework for looped MoE models that improves parameter efficiency, routing health, and pretraining loss without increasing compute or total parameter count.

entry.title: Reasoning with Continuous Latent Diffusion
entry.summary:
Latent Flow Reasoning Models (LFRMs) perform continuous latent diffusion for reasoning by using multi-layer teacher representations, asynchronous denoising, learned prompt encoders, and adapted DiffusionNFT post-training.

Why it matters: LFRMs establish that continuous latent diffusion models can outperform existing continuous-diffusion baselines on complex mathematical and code reasoning tasks using a compact 638M-parameter backbone.

entry.title: Verifier Errors in RLVR: Reward Hacking, Limits of Feedback, and Selective Control
entry.summary:
Researchers mathematically characterize verifier-driven reward hacking in RLVR using gradient flow and introduce an audit-based feedback correction method that achieves selective control to simultaneously reduce accepted errors and increase correctness.

Why it matters: It provides a formal mechanism to prevent language models from exploiting imperfect automated verifiers by using partial human or secondary audits to reduce false positives without degrading model accuracy.

entry.title: MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution
entry.summary:
Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention (MS-GLA) distributes attention heads across multiple temporal resolutions and uses an input-dependent fusion layer, overcoming the single-temporal-resolution memory bottleneck of standard Gated Linear Attention (GLA).

Why it matters: MS-GLA significantly improves long-context generalization and recall performance in linear recurrent models without increasing per-head state memory overhead.

entry.title: Not All Thinking is Created Equal: Latent Reasoning Discovers a Recurrent Search Algorithm for Depth Generalization
entry.summary:
Comparing five GPTNeoX variants on multi-hop reasoning reveals that latent-reasoning models learn a recurrent forward-search algorithm that enables depth generalization to longer reasoning hops, unlike Chain-of-Thought or Pause Token models.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that latent recurrence implements a reusable graph-search algorithm proves that latent reasoning can yield fundamentally better computational abstractions for length generalization than surface-level token traces.

entry.title: Less Sycophancy, Stronger Refusal? Lessons for AI Safety from Mechanistic Interpretability
entry.summary:
Researchers used compensatory feature injection during supervised fine-tuning to suppress sycophancy features in Qwen3.5 models, finding it restores refusal capabilities specifically under user pressure rather than enhancing direct refusal.

Why it matters: Mechanistic interventions that mitigate sycophancy can preserve safety guardrails against user pressure, though they do not automatically broaden baseline direct refusal performance.

entry.title: Beyond Token Scale: Chunk-Level Sparse Autoencoders for Reliable Semantic Feature Discovery
entry.summary:
Chunk-level Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) process mean-pooled activations over contiguous token spans to separate high-level semantic concepts from low-level token features during model interpretability analysis.

Why it matters: By altering what SAEs observe and predict, researchers can extract more reliable semantic features to steer and evaluate language models on complex reasoning and retrieval tasks.

entry.title: Spontaneous Context Restoration: How Language Models Recover from Corrupted Inputs
entry.summary:
Language models exhibit spontaneous context restoration from corrupted inputs via a two-phase internal process that can be predicted early using linear probes.

Why it matters: Early prediction of restoration failures enables efficient failure triage in deployment, saving compute by bypassing unnecessary downstream verification for corrupted inputs.

entry.title: Why Deterministic PRM Guidance Underperforms in Discrete Diffusion Reasoning
entry.summary:
Deterministic Process Reward Model (PRM) guidance underperforms outcome-based reranking in discrete diffusion LLMs when evaluated at equal forward-pass budgets due to weak early-step reward signals and poor final-state scoring.

Why it matters: Effective test-time compute allocation in discrete diffusion models requires preserving early candidate diversity and using final-state verifiers rather than relying on deterministic mid-denoising PRM pruning.
